_readme: THE SHARED-SERVER REGISTER — [pipeline B-1] Private/requirements/ (was pipeline/04-backend-platform.md, folded into the JSON spec 2026-08-15)
The complete set of capabilities the ONE shared `platform` Worker provides — every ROUTE it mounts
and every BINDING any Worker in this repo declares — together with what each one is FOR, who calls
or reads it, and whether it is authenticated.
WHY IT EXISTS. There is exactly one `platform` Worker and one `platform_db` behind the whole
portfolio, so a defect here is not one app's bug — it is every app's outage, including apps that do
not exist yet. SIX other stage-4 requirements quantify over 'the shared capability set' or 'every
binding', and until this file landed that set did not exist. An undefined right-hand side cannot
reject anything, so all six reported clean over nothing:
[4]B-2   onboarding an app is DATA, not a source edit    -> the route set this must not change
[4]B-3   the server can authenticate a caller            -> auth: required must be non-zero
[4]B-4a  every written row belongs to a registered app   -> the write routes, enumerated
[4]B-13  no unauthenticated route can be made expensive  -> auth: public x limiter, below
[4]B-14  every field of every shared route is pinned     -> the route count is the pair floor
[4]B-18  one shared bucket, every bucket has a reader    -> bindings[], and its reader limb
🔴 THE ONE RULE THAT MAKES THIS FILE MEAN ANYTHING: MEMBERSHIP IS NOT A CLAIM, RESOLUTION IS.
Writing `"client": "TBD"` was the original acceptance criterion's third limb, and a string field is
satisfied by any string. Every `client` here is an EXPRESSION that must appear in comment-stripped
source in a file OUTSIDE the serving Worker, and must itself contain the route's own static path —
so a client entry cannot be satisfied by the server's own declaration of the route, and cannot
survive the route being renamed. `_registerInWorkspace` matched its own declaration six times in
this repo; this is the seventh place that was not allowed to happen.
Enforced by tooling/ci/assert-platform-register.mjs:
· LIMB 1 route set == what services/platform/src/index.ts MOUNTS, parsed (following app.route()
into each sub-router), in BOTH directions                                            [B-1]
· LIMB 2 a route with no client is NOT a build failure — it PRINTS its `unconsumedReason` on
every run, and the reason must be non-empty. Same shape as
assert-capability-register.mjs's zero-consumer rule                                   [B-1]
· LIMB 3 binding set == every `d1_databases`/`kv_namespaces`/`r2_buckets`/`ratelimits` entry
across services/*/wrangler.jsonc AND the brick template, in BOTH directions; each must have a
REAL READER — `env.<BINDING>` in comment-stripped code in a file that is NOT the Env type
declaration                                                                    [B-1, B-18]
· LIMB 4 every `auth: public` route reaches withinRateLimit/withinEdgeCeiling at a real call site
in its owningFile, or declares a `noLimiterReason` that prints on every run          [B-13]
· LIMB 5 every value in `sharedValues` below is carried by EVERY config in `bindingSources`,
at exactly the declared value; absence fails unless the entry's `absentFrom` names that
config with a reason, and an `absentFrom` row for a config that DOES carry it fails too
(added 2026-09-08 — see that block's own _why for the mutation measurement)
⚠️ COVERAGE IS A RELATIONSHIP, NEVER A NUMBER. The route floor is 'equals what index.ts mounts' and
the binding floor is 'equals what the wrangler configs declare' — both derived from files CI already
parses. There is no tuned integer anyone can lower. The one integer in the guard is a self-check
that the PARSE still finds routes at all, because a parser that matches nothing reports perfect
agreement with an empty register.
⚠️ NOT tooling/capability-register.json. That file is the PACKAGE register (stage 2/3): Dart
packages, seams and their consumers. This one is the SERVER's. They are deliberately separate files
because they answer to different guards, different stages and different trees — merging them would
make one guard's coverage floor depend on the other's subject.
🔴 TWO WORKERS, TWO ARRAYS, ONE DERIVED SET (2026-08-25). `routes[]` is the SHARED host’s and
`appWorkers[].routes` is each per-app backend’s. Until this landed, limb 1’s subject was
`servingWorker` alone, so services/subscriptiontracker-api’s TWELVE mounted handlers were in no register at all
and limb 2 covered none of them. The Worker set is now READ OFF THE TREE — every `services/*`
wrangler config declaring `main` — and the register must name exactly that set in both directions,
so a third backend cannot arrive unnoticed. The route key is (worker, method, path): both Workers
mount GET /v1/health and DELETE /v1/account, and both are real, different routes.

_why: The Worker whose mounted routes the register's `routes` array must equal, exactly. Named as data
rather than hardcoded in the guard so that the guard fails loudly if this Worker is renamed or
moved, instead of quietly scanning a path that no longer exists.
servingWorker.name: platform

_why: services/subscriptiontracker-api — the ONE per-app backend in the portfolio, and until 2026-08-25 the only
deployable Worker in this repo whose mounted routes no register named. It answers on
api.nikatru.com and mounts TWELVE handlers; `routes[]` above held nine, all of them the shared
host's, so limb 2's rule — 'a capability with no client is not delivered' — covered none of
these. A handler deleted from this Worker and a handler that never existed produced the same
observation, which is exactly the condition GET /v1/renewals lived in: 108 lines, mounted behind
supabaseAuth, covered by its own test file, and called by nothing in any language.
⚠️ KEPT IN A SEPARATE ARRAY FROM `routes`, ON PURPOSE. `routes[]` is the SHARED SERVER’s
capability set and tooling/ci/assert-analytics-contract.mjs quantifies over exactly that set for
[4]B-14's wire pins — one contract per shared route, in both directions. Folding a per-app
Worker's routes into it would silently redefine that other guard's subject and demand a wire
pin for every Subly endpoint, which is a different requirement about a different tree.
THE WORKER LIST ITSELF IS DERIVED, NOT LISTED: assert-platform-register.mjs reads every
`services/*` wrangler config that declares `main` and requires the register to name exactly that
set, in both directions. A third backend cannot arrive here unnoticed.
⚠️ WHAT LIMB 2 CHECKS, STATED SO NOBODY READS MORE INTO A GREEN THAN IS THERE: the rule is that
the route’s URL is BUILT by code outside the serving Worker and that the expression carries the
route’s own path. It is not reachability analysis. Three entries here resolve a real client and
were then measured one level further by hand — PATCH /v1/subscriptions/:id, PUT /v1/budget and
GET /v1/entitlements each build their URL in dio_api_client.dart through a SubscriptionRepository
method that nothing in apps/subscriptiontracker calls. That is written into each note rather than left implied,
because "a declaration counted as a call" is this repo’s most repeated defect and a register that
hid it would be the seventh place it happened.
appWorkers.name: subscriptiontracker-api
appWorkers._nameWhy: THE DEPLOYED WORKER NAME. assert-platform-register.mjs compares this field against `name` in the config below. Until 2026-09-11 the deployed name was the retired `subly-api` while the directory and slug were already `subscriptiontracker`; [ADR 079] moved the deployed name to match, as a new Worker that claimed both custom domains on its first deploy.
_clientBasePathWhy: Subly's Dart seam is constructed with `baseUrl: '${AppConfig.apiBaseUrl}/v1'`
(apps/subscriptiontracker/lib/state/providers/subscriptions.dart:52), so every call site in dio_api_client.dart names the
path BELOW /v1 — `_rest.get('/budget')`, not `/v1/budget`. Requiring the full path in the client
expression would have made ten honest clients unresolvable and pushed them into
`unconsumedReason`, which is how a real client becomes a written excuse. The guard does not take
this on trust: the prefix must front EVERY route this Worker mounts and must leave a non-empty
residual, so it cannot be widened until it swallows the segment the rename check depends on.

routes.purpose: Deploy verification AND dependency health for the per-app Worker. Answers `{ ok, status, app, version, build, time, checks }` after probing APP_DB (`SELECT 1 FROM subscriptions LIMIT 1`), PLATFORM_DB (`SELECT 1 FROM entitlements LIMIT 1`) and the Supabase JWKS, each through a per-isolate memoised reading (services/_shared/src/health.ts); JWKS_CACHE is deliberately NOT probed (services/subscriptiontracker-api/src/index.ts says why). ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-09-10 — this field described a vars-only answer that touched no dependency while the handler probed three. `build` is the commit this Worker was deployed from and is what joins a deploy to a running binary; `version` is the literal API-contract version. [pipeline 14]O-7.

client.note: The `--url` argument of the post-deploy smoke step, which fails the deploy job unless this route answers `ok:true` at the deployed sha. It is a MACHINE consumer, not a human one — the same script smokes services/platform's health route from the step below it.

routes.noLimiterReason: It DOES I/O — two D1 reads (APP_DB, PLATFORM_DB) and one JWKS subrequest — and what bounds it is the per-isolate MEMO, not a limiter: each probe is a reading with a TTL (services/_shared/src/health.ts, READING_TTL_MS = 5 s for D1, JWKS_READING_TTL_MS for the JWKS fetch), so a flood buys at most one fan-out per TTL per isolate, (isolates × 1 per TTL) in total, and every other request costs the Worker invocation itself, which the account-wide request ceiling already bounds. Identical reasoning to the shared host’s health route, and corrected on the same day (2026-09-10) for the same reason: the field claimed the handler touched no dependency at all while it probed three, and limb 4b of assert-platform-register.mjs now refuses that claim. [4]B-13

routes.purpose: G2 erasure for subscriptiontracker_db. THE ONE ROUTE ON THIS WORKER BEHIND THE STRICT BOUNDARY: mounted under `erasureAuth` (ES256/JWKS only, no HS256 fallback) and it re-checks `tokenAssurance` itself, so moving the mount produces a logged 403 rather than a silent downgrade. The table set is DERIVED from the schema (a `user_id` column is the selector), never a literal list.

client.note: The relay. THE CALLER IS THE SHARED HOST, NOT THE APP: the Dart seam calls platform’s /v1/account once, and platform checks the service-role precondition, empties platform_db, relays to each app’s own DELETE /v1/account, and deletes the identity LAST. That ordering is the safety property, which is why the client must not own it (apps/subscriptiontracker/lib/state/providers/auth.dart:63-101 records the same thing from the other side).

routes.purpose: Every subscription owned by the verified user, newest renewal first. Scoped by the token's user_id, never by a body value.

client.note: The real call inside `getSubscriptions()`, at the assignment — not the class doc comment, which is stripped before matching.

routes.purpose: Create one subscription for the verified user. Validates the whole body before any write and answers 201 with the stored row.

client.note: The first positional argument of the real `_rest.post` call inside `createSubscription()`.

routes.purpose: One subscription the user owns, plus its `payment_history` rows. The ownership predicate is in the SQL (`AND user_id = ?`), so a row belonging to someone else is a 404 rather than a filtered read.

client.note: Two methods share this route: `getSubscription()` reads the subscription half and `getPaymentHistory()` reads the `payment_history` half of the same body.

routes.purpose: Update a WHITELISTED field set on a subscription the user owns. Unknown keys are refused rather than ignored.

client.note: The real call inside `updateSubscription()`. ⚠️ MEASURED 2026-08-25 AND WORTH SAYING PLAINLY: the URL is built here, which is what limb 2 checks and it is genuinely the code that would issue this request — but the method that builds it has no live caller. `SubscriptionRepository.update` (apps/subscriptiontracker/lib/data/subscriptions/subscription_repository.dart:14) wraps it and NOTHING calls that wrapper: the only three repository methods reached from the UI or the controller are `fetchAll`, `add`, `cancel`, `history` and `budget`. So the route is reachable in code and not reached in the shipped app. Recorded rather than smoothed over — "a declaration counted as a call" is the exact defect services/subscriptiontracker-api/README.md warns about two paragraphs before it makes the same mistake.

routes.purpose: Delete one subscription the user owns. Ownership is in the SQL, so a foreign id deletes nothing and says so.
The upcoming-renewals list for the verified user, computed server-side over a window. Mounted at index.ts:87 behind `supabaseAuth`, 108 lines, with its own test file.
routes.unconsumedReason: 🔴 NOTHING IN THIS REPO CALLS IT, AND THAT IS THE FINDING THIS ENTRY EXISTS TO STOP BEING INVISIBLE. Measured 2026-08-25 across every language and every root in the repo, with the /v1 prefix removed after that exact mistake once produced a false negative: apps/subscriptiontracker/lib/data/api/api_client.dart declares NINE methods and none is renewals; dio_api_client.dart issues NINE requests and none is to /renewals; packages/api_client has no renewals transport; and every bare-word `renewals` hit outside services/ is a UI string, a feature flag, the platform cron fan-out (services/platform/src/scheduled.ts, which writes subscriptiontracker_db DIRECTLY through the SUBSCRIPTIONTRACKER_DB binding and never over HTTP), or a test. The app computes its upcoming-renewal list locally from the subscriptions it already holds. ⚠️ IT IS NOT DELETED, AND DELETION IS NOT THIS ITEM’S CALL: it is a plausible sync-era surface, deletion is the irreversible half, and the register’s whole purpose is that an unconsumed capability is a PRINTED fact rather than a silence. Give it a client or remove it deliberately — but from now on the choice is on the screen every CI run.

routes.purpose: The user's monthly budget and per-category caps, with defaults when nothing is stored. Returns each category's surrogate `id` (0002_schema_debt.sql) so a category is addressable as (entity, row_id) outside the database.

REPLACE the budget and the whole category set, validated before any write and issued as ONE `APP_DB.batch()` so the DELETE cannot commit without its inserts. A category id supplied by the caller is PRESERVED, so a rename is an edit rather than a delete+create.

client.note: The real call inside `updateBudget()`. ⚠️ MEASURED 2026-08-25 AND WORTH SAYING PLAINLY: the URL is built here, which is what limb 2 checks and it is genuinely the code that would issue this request — but the method that builds it has no live caller. `SubscriptionRepository.saveBudget` (subscription_repository.dart:19) wraps it and has no caller; `budget_screen.dart:20` reads the budget and nothing writes one back yet. The route is complete, tested and unreached.

routes.purpose: Subly's mount of THE ONE entitlement reader — services/_shared/src/entitlement-read.ts, since 2026-09-10 — scoped by the verified user_id and this deploy's APP_ID. Until that day this route carried its OWN `SELECT … FROM entitlements` with no bundle branch, so a live bundle grant answered `is_pro: false` here and `is_pro: true` on the shared host for the same user and rows; the answer is now byte-identical to `GET platform.nikatru.com/v1/entitlements?app_id=<APP_ID>` (services/platform/test/one-entitlement-reader.test.ts drives one fixture through both), and tooling/ci/assert-one-entitlement-reader.mjs refuses a second reader. Predates the shared host’s /v1/entitlements ([ADR 020]) and is why that route’s _why paragraph calls this “the one legacy app that happens to have a backend”. The money boundary fails closed on every undecidable case, including a row whose money environment is not this deploy’s ([5]M-12).

client.note: The real call inside `getEntitlements()`. Note that the SHARED host’s identically-pathed route has a DIFFERENT client (packages/api_client/lib/src/dio_entitlement_transport.dart) — which is precisely why the route key had to become (worker, method, path). ⚠️ MEASURED 2026-08-25 AND WORTH SAYING PLAINLY: the URL is built here, which is what limb 2 checks and it is genuinely the code that would issue this request — but the method that builds it has no live caller. `SubscriptionRepository.entitlements()` (subscription_repository.dart:20) wraps it and its only other occurrence in the app tree is a doc comment in apps/subscriptiontracker/test/width_calendar_test.dart:630. services/subscriptiontracker-api/README.md already calls this one of "two routes with zero clients, kept on purpose" — this entry is where that claim stops being prose that can rot.

_why: Every config whose bindings the register must account for. DERIVED at runtime by globbing
services/*/wrangler.jsonc plus the brick's service template — this list is the guard's COVERAGE
assertion, not its input: if the glob finds a config that is not named here, or names one the
glob cannot find, the scan and the tree have diverged and the build fails.
The brick template is IN SCOPE on purpose. assert-clone-contract.mjs inspects only the throwaway
CI probe stamp, so services/subscriptiontracker-api is invisible to it — which is exactly how a per-app R2
bucket stayed live from 2026-07-17 with every guard green.
🔴 THE VALUES THAT ARE TYPED INTO ALL THREE WRANGLER CONFIGS, DECLARED ONCE, HERE.
`bindingSources.configs` above is the complete set of Worker configs in this repository. Four
values were typed identically into all three of them and NOTHING compared them:
vars.SUPABASE_URL                      one identity project for the whole portfolio
vars.API_VERSION                       one API-contract version
d1_databases[PLATFORM_DB].database_id  one entitlements database
kv_namespaces[JWKS_CACHE].id           one JWKS cache namespace
⚠️ WHAT WAS ALREADY GUARDED, SAID FIRST SO THIS BLOCK IS NOT CREDITED WITH IT.
tooling/ci/assert-d1-bindings.mjs already holds database_name and database_id in agreement — but
its subject is DEPLOYABLE configs under services/ and its header says so, deliberately, because
the template correctly carries an all-zeros APP_DB placeholder. So PLATFORM_DB's id was compared
between the two live Workers and NOT against the template. tooling/ci/assert-data-inventory.mjs
pins the JWKS namespace id from the legal inventory. SUPABASE_URL and API_VERSION were compared
by nothing, anywhere.
MUTATION-MEASURED 2026-09-08, before this block existed, each value changed on its own in the
brick template and the FULL sweep (tooling/scripts/guard-sweep.mjs, 134 guards executed) run
against clean and against mutated:
SUPABASE_URL      -> a foreign Supabase project   RED set UNCHANGED (nothing saw it)
API_VERSION       -> "v9"                          RED set UNCHANGED (nothing saw it)
PLATFORM_DB id    -> a fabricated uuid             RED set UNCHANGED (nothing saw it)
JWKS_CACHE id     -> a fabricated namespace id     assert-data-inventory.mjs RED (the only catch)
And in the LIVE Worker services/subscriptiontracker-api, repointing SUPABASE_URL at a foreign project and
bumping API_VERSION to "v9" both passed every one of those guards too. A stamped backend would
have verified tokens against a project that does not exist and read entitlements from the wrong
database, with CI green.
⚠️ ASSERTED, NOT GENERATED, AND THAT IS A DECISION RATHER THAN THE EASIER PATH. These three files
are hand-written configuration whose comments carry the REASONS for what they declare; a
generator that rewrote them would own that prose too, and prose a generator owns is prose nobody
writes. The corpus already asserts rather than generates on exactly this class
(assert-d1-bindings.mjs, assert-cors-allowlist.mjs), and the property wanted here is that a
divergence is RED — which an assertion delivers with nothing to regenerate and nothing to forget
to regenerate.
⚠️ WHY `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` IS NOT IN THIS LIST, THOUGH IT TOO IS COPIED INTO ALL THREE. It is not a
shared VALUE. It is per-Worker and DERIVED from catalog/apps.json by
tooling/ci/assert-cors-allowlist.mjs, which requires an exact set per Worker in BOTH directions
and already refuses an origin nothing justifies. Declaring one literal for it here would replace
a derivation with a copy — the defect this block exists to close, committed in the other
direction. The two live lists deliberately DIFFER (services/platform carries
http://localhost:3000 and services/subscriptiontracker-api does not, because subscriptiontracker-api's middleware allows any
localhost by regex and platform's has none); that asymmetry is recorded at
services/subscriptiontracker-api/src/middleware/cors.ts:20-27 and enforced by that guard's EXTRAS.
GRAMMAR of `at`, and it is the entire addressing scheme:
vars.<NAME>                      -> cfg.vars[<NAME>]
<section>[<BINDING>].<field>     -> the entry of cfg[<section>] whose `binding` is <BINDING>
An `at` this grammar cannot parse is COVERAGE LOST, never a pass.
Enforced by tooling/ci/assert-platform-register.mjs LIMB 5:
· every config in `bindingSources.configs` must carry every entry below, at EXACTLY the
declared value — a divergence is a failure, in both directions;
· an entry absent from a config is a failure UNLESS that config is named in the entry's
`absentFrom` with a reason — and an `absentFrom` row for a config that DOES carry the value
is itself a failure, so an exemption cannot outlive the state it describes;
· an entry that resolves in ZERO configs is COVERAGE LOST, so a renamed key silently removing
the subject cannot read as a pass.

values.why: ONE Supabase identity project (Cross_Platform_Auth, ap-south-1) for the whole portfolio, so one issuer, one JWKS document and one user row per human across every app. A Worker pointed at a second project verifies tokens nobody in this portfolio can mint — every authenticated route 401s while the Worker itself is perfectly well, which is the failure services/subscriptiontracker-api's health probe `supabase_jwks` exists to make visible and which no static check could see.

The API-contract version every Worker serves under `/v1` and reports in its health body. tooling/capability-register.json records that it is the literal "v1" in both Workers and has never changed — which is precisely why assert-worker-error-sink.mjs FAILS a crash sink that uses it as a release id. Two Workers disagreeing about it would mean one of them mounts routes the clients do not call and reports a version its deploy smoke does not expect.

The ONE entitlements database for the portfolio ([ADR 057]'s union lives inside it). services/platform is the sole migrations applier; every other Worker binds it read/write with no migrations_dir. A Worker bound to a different id deploys, runs, and reads and writes the WRONG database silently — the exact shape assert-d1-bindings.mjs was written for between the two live configs, extended here to the template that every future backend is stamped from.

One identity project means one public JWKS document, so a second namespace would be a second copy of one public file — doubling the KV writes that cache costs against the budget tooling/ceilings.json records as kv.writesPerDay. tooling/legal/data-inventory.json also pins this id, which is why a mutation here is the one of the four an existing guard already caught; that guard answers a legal question about a store of data, not the portfolio-agreement question this entry answers.

routes.purpose: Deploy verification AND dependency health. Answers `{ ok, status, app, version, build, time, checks }` after probing PLATFORM_DB (`SELECT 1 FROM entitlements LIMIT 1`), CONFIG_KV (a `get` of a key that does not exist) and the Supabase JWKS, each through a per-isolate memoised reading (services/_shared/src/health.ts); HTTP 200 even when `ok` is false, by design, so the judgement stays with the reader. ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-09-10 — this field described a vars-only answer that touched no dependency, for as long as the probes had existed (services/platform/src/index.ts:115-144).
routes.unconsumedReason: 🔄 CORRECTED 2026-08-06 — IT HAS A MACHINE CONSUMER AND HAS FOR SOME TIME. `tooling/ops/post-deploy-smoke.mjs` fetches this route from `deploy-workers.yml` (twice, both Workers) and joins the deploy to a build through the `build` field; `deploy-web.yml` smokes it too. The previous text — "no programmatic client by design … the honest state is zero clients" — was true when written and false at head, and it PRINTED GREEN every run because limb 2 only reports unconsumed reasons rather than checking them. [4]B-14 now pins the field set the smoke joins on.
routes.noLimiterReason: It DOES I/O — one D1 read, one KV read and one JWKS subrequest — and what bounds it is not a limiter but the MEMO: every probe is a per-isolate reading with a TTL (services/_shared/src/health.ts, READING_TTL_MS = 5 s for D1 and KV, JWKS_READING_TTL_MS for the JWKS fetch), so an unauthenticated flood buys at most one dependency fan-out per TTL per isolate — a bound health.ts states as (isolates × 1 per TTL), deliberately not as a global one — and every other request costs the Worker invocation itself, which the account-wide request ceiling already bounds. A limiter here would spend a Rate Limiting namespace to protect a memoised read. ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-09-10: from the day the probes landed this field claimed the handler touched neither D1, nor KV, nor the network, and limb 4 of assert-platform-register.mjs printed it green because it checked only that a reason was PRESENT; limb 4b now refuses that claim over a handler that probes. [4]B-13

routes.purpose: CFG-1 runtime config: compiled-in defaults overlaid with a KV override (`config:<app>`), edge-cached 300s. DATA and flags only, never server-driven UI, never secrets.

client.note: The URL the transport actually builds, at the assignment — not the doc comment three lines above it, which says the same thing and is stripped before matching.

routes.purpose: G-12 first-party analytics ingest ([ADR 011]). Batched, pseudonymous, consent-gated CLIENT-side. Unauthenticated deliberately: the most valuable events (first_launch, paywall_viewed) happen before any login exists, and a bearer token would attach an identity to rows whose whole point is that they carry none.

client.note: The first positional argument of the real `_dio.post` call.

routes.purpose: The DPDP consent artifact each analytics event references. Append-only: a withdrawal is a NEW row with granted=0, never an UPDATE, because the audit trail is the point (DPDP §6(3)).

client.note: The first positional argument of the real `_dio.post` call.

routes.purpose: G2 in-app account deletion ([4]B-5). THE FIRST `auth: required` ROUTE ON THIS WORKER, and the reason src/middleware/auth.ts is not a dead file. Three limbs: every user-owned table in platform_db (DERIVED from the schema — a `user_id` column is the selector — not from a literal array somebody must remember to extend), then the identity record itself. Refuses 501 while SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY is unset, so it ships honest rather than not at all.
routes.unconsumedReason: 🔄 CORRECTED 2026-08-06 — THE CLIENT HALF EXISTS. `packages/core/lib/src/auth/account_deletion.dart` models the three refusals this route answers with, `packages/auth_supabase/lib/src/supabase_auth_repository.dart:43` calls `DELETE /v1/account`, and `packages/core/test/account_deletion_test.dart` covers the 501. The claim that it was "blocked on stage 2" was true when written and false at head. [4]B-14 pins the STATUS SET rather than a body, because this route's client reads no body key — `AccountDeletionFailure.forStatus` is the contract.

routes.purpose: ⏱ 2026-09-16 · O-SIWA-TOKEN-NOT-REVOKED-ON-DELETE. KEEPS THE ONE VALUE THE DELETION ABOVE CANNOT BE DONE WITHOUT: Apple's own refresh token for this account. Apple requires an app offering Sign in with Apple to revoke the user's tokens when the account is deleted, and 'POST https://appleid.apple.com/auth/revoke' takes a token; the identity provider hands it to the CLIENT once, on the session that completes the OAuth redirect, and stores none of it (supabase/auth#1308 is closed as not planned). So the app posts it here. ⏱ 2026-09-24 · O-GOOGLE-SIGN-IN-NOT-BUILT: now the Apple ALIAS of PUT /v1/account/provider-token below, unchanged on the wire (`{refreshToken, appId}`), kept because the web client shipped on 2026-09-22 sends here; it writes platform_db.provider_tokens with provider = 'apple', and is refused (400) for an account whose verified token does not list apple. The response is a COUNT. The token is never logged, never echoed and readable by no route — its only reader is src/lib/provider-revoke.ts.
routes.unconsumedReason: CONSUMED: packages/core/lib/src/auth/provider_token_keeper.dart (keepProviderRefreshToken, and the Apple-only keepAppleRefreshToken the template wires) posts Apple's token through packages/api_client/lib/src/account_deletion_request.dart (storeAppleRefreshToken), wired in both trees by appleTokenKeeperProvider and proven in services/platform/test/provider-revoke.test.ts and services/platform/test/provider-token.test.ts.

routes.purpose: ⏱ 2026-09-24 · O-GOOGLE-SIGN-IN-NOT-BUILT. The provider-general form of the route above: body `{provider, refreshToken, appId}`, `provider` one of `apple` / `google` and cross-checked against the verified token's `app_metadata.providers` (a provider the account has not linked is 400). platform_db.provider_tokens keeps one row per (subject, provider) until DELETE /v1/account revokes it — at Apple, or at Google through 'POST https://oauth2.googleapis.com/revoke', which takes the token and no client credential. The subject is the JWT's, never the body's; the response is a COUNT; the token is never logged, never echoed and readable by no route — its only reader is src/lib/provider-revoke.ts.
routes.unconsumedReason: CONSUMED: apps/subscriptiontracker/lib/state/providers/auth.dart (sendProviderRefreshToken, wired into appleTokenKeeperProvider) posts every non-Apple provider token through packages/api_client/lib/src/account_deletion_request.dart (storeProviderRefreshToken). No shipped build produces one yet: Google sign-in is the Dart half of O-GOOGLE-SIGN-IN-NOT-BUILT. Proven in services/platform/test/provider-token.test.ts.

routes.purpose: [pipeline 5]M-4 — ANY app reads ITS entitlement from the host every stamped app already has. The brick's DEFAULT stamp is CLIENT-ONLY ([ADR 020]), so until this route existed the only working entitlement read in the repo was inside services/subscriptiontracker-api — i.e. inside the one legacy app that happens to have a backend, while every app the factory stamps had no way to ask whether its user had paid. Scoped by BOTH user_id (from the verified token) AND app_id (a required query parameter that must name a registered app); the money boundary fails closed on every undecidable case, including a row whose money environment is not this deploy's ([5]M-12). ⏱ 2026-09-10 — the read itself no longer lives in this file: it is services/_shared/src/entitlement-read.ts, THE ONE READER ([ADR 057] §5), which services/subscriptiontracker-api mounts too; this route validates nothing the reader does not and renders the reader's answer into the envelope [4]B-14 pins.
routes.unconsumedReason: 🔄 CORRECTED 2026-08-06 — THERE IS A DART CLIENT. `packages/api_client/lib/src/dio_entitlement_transport.dart:40` issues `GET {platformBaseUrl}/v1/entitlements?app_id=<id>` as a `core.EntitlementTransport`. The claim of "no Dart client yet … nothing fetches" was true when written and false at head. [4]B-14 pins the three envelope keys plus the ten-key row item.
routes.noLimiterReason: NOT APPLICABLE — `auth: required`, so limb 4 does not range over it. Recorded anyway because the read is on a launch path and the 100k Worker-requests/day Free ceiling is ACCOUNT-WIDE across ~50 apps: this must never become a per-screen fetch, which is a client-side constraint the cache in packages/core exists to satisfy.

routes.purpose: [ADR 057] §5 — "what do I own", which the per-app route cannot answer. `/v1/entitlements?app_id=X` is scoped to ONE app by design and every shipped client depends on that scoping, so widening it would change a released contract; adding a route changes nothing that exists. It answers the subject-wide union — the per-app rows plus the products of every live bundle grant, deduped with the per-app branch winning — through the SAME `grantsAccess` five rules, the same auth and the same 503 when MONEY_ENVIRONMENT is undeclared. It carries `bundle_grants.source` per grant, which is what makes "manage your subscription where you bought it" an honest sentence: cross-rail cancellation is impossible by construction on every store rail.
routes.unconsumedReason: NO DART CLIENT FETCHES IT YET, and that is a state rather than a construction. The account page is what will; `packages/api_client` builds `/v1/entitlements?app_id=` only. Its four envelope keys are DECLARED SERVER-ONLY in tooling/ci/assert-analytics-contract.mjs with the reason each — an undeclared extra is indistinguishable from a field somebody forgot to wire up, which is exactly the [4]B-14 failure. ⚠️ THE ACCESS DECISION IS NOT HERE: `is_pro` on the per-app route is what every client reads and it is deliberately unchanged, so nothing about this route can lock anyone out.
routes.noLimiterReason: NOT APPLICABLE — `auth: required`, so limb 4 does not range over it. Recorded anyway because it is a heavier read than the per-app route (one query per live grant to resolve pinned members) against an ACCOUNT-WIDE 100k Worker-requests/day ceiling shared by ~50 apps: it is an account-page read, never a per-screen one.

routes.purpose: ⏱ 2026-09-24 · O-EXTENSION-ACCOUNT-CHECK-UNBUILT (design §3.2, §3.4). The signed-in page https://nikatru.com/ext/connect mints a 120-second, single-use code for the browser extension, bound to {product, channel, redirect_uri, code_challenge} (PKCE S256 only). `platformAuth` is carried AT THE HANDLER, not by an `app.use`, so it cannot leak onto a sibling path. It refuses a product other than `fullshot`, a channel other than the three extension store rows, a channel whose `extensionRedirectUri` in tooling/channel-register.json is null (all three today — the dark launch), and a redirect_uri not byte-equal to that register value. It answers {code, redirect_uri} with the REGISTER's value, so the page can never be steered to a URL of the caller's choosing.

client.note: The URL the connect page POSTs to, at its one declaration — the page builds no other platform URL.

routes.noLimiterReason: NOT APPLICABLE — `auth: required`, so limb 4 does not range over it. One INSERT per sign-in by an authenticated user.

routes.purpose: ⏱ 2026-09-24 · O-EXTENSION-ACCOUNT-CHECK-UNBUILT. The extension exchanges {code, code_verifier, redirect_uri} for {token, link_id}. No Supabase session: the one-time code IS the credential, consumed by ONE atomic UPDATE (single use, now < expires_at), then checked against the stored S256 challenge and the byte-exact redirect_uri. Every failure answers the same `invalid_grant` body. The token (`nkx1_…`) is returned once and only its SHA-256 is stored. Behind EXT_TOKEN_CEILING_LIMITER, keyed on the edge, never an IP.
routes.unconsumedReason: THE CLIENT ARRIVES IN PR-X, the extension half (extensions/Extension/Full_Screen_Shot pro/pro.js and background.js), which this PR deliberately does not touch. Until the parent fills a measured `extensionRedirectUri` no code can be minted in production, so no caller can reach a 200 here; the route is live and inert.

routes.purpose: ⏱ 2026-09-24 · O-EXTENSION-ACCOUNT-CHECK-UNBUILT (ADR 059 D7: revocation per session). A device credential revokes ITSELF — `revoked_at` on the calling device only, named by its own credential hash. `extDeviceAuth` is carried AT THE HANDLER. Required auth here is the DEVICE credential, not a JWT: a JWT is refused. After it, that credential answers 401 everywhere, which is the extension's signal to delete it.
routes.unconsumedReason: THE CLIENT ARRIVES IN PR-X, the extension half (sign-out in the options page), which this PR deliberately does not touch.
routes.noLimiterReason: NOT APPLICABLE — `auth: required` (the device credential), so limb 4 does not range over it. One guarded UPDATE by an authenticated device.

routes.purpose: [pipeline 5]M-9 — the user-initiated cancel path. Mounted behind app.use('/v1/plan/*', platformAuth), so the subscription is resolved from the VERIFIED SESSION and never from the request body; the body carries only app_id. Writes an append-only cancellation_requests row (migration 0005) rather than mutating entitlements in place, so a cancel is a fact with a timestamp instead of a state change that loses its own history. 202 is a success and the common case: the host records the request and answers 202 when it could not also execute it against the merchant of record synchronously.

client.note: The URL the transport actually builds, at the post() call site — not the doc comment on line 5, which names the same path and is stripped before matching.

routes.purpose: O-PLAY-AI-CONTENT-REPORTING (MASTER_PLAN G-39) — the in-app report of AI-generated content that Google Play requires of any app that generates content with AI ("report or flag offensive content to developers without needing to exit the app", answer/13985936). Mounted behind app.use('/v1/report', platformAuth): the reporter is the verified JWT subject, never a body field. Validates app_id against the catalogue and reason against a closed set, caps each person at 10 reports an hour (a D1 read, not a binding), stores a content_reports row (migration 0013), answers 202, and sends a capped, content-free support notice under waitUntil.

client.note: The URL the transport builds at the post() call site. O-PLAY-AI-CONTENT-REPORTING chassis half: the brick opens it from Settings when AppConfig.generatesAiContent is true, and from a generated item through showReportContentDialog.

routes.purpose: [pipeline 5]M-1 — the ONE door a merchant of record knocks on. Verifies an HMAC-SHA256 signature over the RAW body with the rail's per-destination secret, records the notification verbatim exactly once, acks, then derives the entitlement. [ADR 020]:18 puts it on the SHARED host because a per-app Worker must never see a webhook: fifty stamped apps inherit one verified rail rather than fifty copies of a signature check. [ADR 004] fixes the merchant of record as Paddle, and the adapter registry is what makes a successor a config change. ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-08-28: this read ‘as Paddle / Lemon Squeezy’. [ADR 039] D4 (2026-08-09) RETIRED [ADR 004]’s parallel Lemon Squeezy clause — never evidenced, and the product is sunsetting into Stripe — so the registry holds exactly one rail today.
routes.unconsumedReason: NO CLIENT IN THIS REPO, BY CONSTRUCTION — the caller is the merchant of record's own delivery system, not any code we ship. This is the one route whose 'who calls it' answer is a vendor, and the honest state is zero in-tree clients. What replaces the client check for this route is tooling/ci/assert-mor-adapters.mjs, which asserts the verifier exists, is CALLED, and is the only path to an entitlements write across ALL of services/**.
routes.noLimiterReason: It DOES reach withinEdgeCeiling (MONEY_CEILING_LIMITER) — this field is present only to record why the ceiling is the server-derived one and not the fairness bucket: there is no per-install identity on a webhook to be fair between, and the only meaningful key is one the caller cannot choose.

routes.purpose: The Paddle CREATE-TRANSACTION server half ([ADR 044]). Creates a DRAFT transaction from `items` alone and returns its `checkout.url`. 🔴 THE SHAPE IS THE SAFETY PROPERTY: the create body type carries NO settable `status` field at all, so passing `status:"billed"` is a COMPILE ERROR rather than a code-review catch. That matters because `billed` mints an invoice number and an immutable tax record, and on a cardless trial Paddle auto-completes the transaction and creates a subscription — removing the human from a loop everything else here assumes.
routes.unconsumedReason: ⚠️ NOTHING CALLS THIS ROUTE TODAY, AND THAT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN DRESSED UP. [ADR 044] §5(2) found that `Paddle.Checkout.open({items})` opens a checkout with NO server-created transaction and NO API key on the request path, exercising the identical payment-link and `_ptxn` machinery — "the server endpoint is therefore not a v1 dependency, which was the load-bearing surprise of this investigation". The owner then chose BOTH rungs, so this exists as rung 2. It earns its place the moment a transaction needs something the overlay cannot pre-fill: a known `customer_id`, a discount, or `custom_data` carrying our own account id — and §6 records that last one as a FILED DEFECT, not a nicety. Until then this is an UNCONSUMED route by design, and the honest state is zero clients.

routes.purpose: 🔴 THE ROUTE THAT REMOVES THE IRREVERSIBLE CLIENT UNLOCK. A store purchase must never grant on the strength of the client's word, and never on the push alone: Google's RTDN carries no proof in its body (purchases.subscriptionsv2.get is mandatory) and Microsoft Store has no push at all. The client posts an OPAQUE token; the SERVER calls the store's own API; only a verified server-side answer writes a bundle grant. That is what makes the purchase→unlock loop testable without the leg that, on iOS and Android, cannot be reversed. It also carries the double-billing pre-check: 409 already_entitled NAMES the holding rail before a store call is spent, so a person who owns the set on another rail is told where.
routes.unconsumedReason: NO DART CLIENT POSTS TO IT YET, and that is a state rather than a construction: no rail has a credential minted, so every verifier answers 503 in this deploy and there is nothing for a client to succeed at. The purchase surface arrives with the store rails. There is therefore no released client of ours to break and no wire contract to pin; what stands in for one is tooling/ci/assert-bundle-provenance.mjs, which asserts every writer into bundle_grants is downstream of a verification seam and that no grant-deciding field derives from a request body.
routes.noLimiterReason: NOT APPLICABLE — `auth: required`, so limb 4 does not range over it. Recorded anyway because it is the one authenticated route that makes an OUTBOUND call per request: a retry loop here spends a store API quota as well as the account-wide 100k Worker-requests/day ceiling, and the honest bound is that a verified receipt is written once and re-posting the same token is an upsert, not a second pull.

bindings.purpose: The ONE entitlements + analytics + consent database for the whole portfolio. services/platform is the SOLE migrations applier; every other Worker binds it without a migrations_dir.

Subly's own database, bound into `platform` READ/WRITE for the nightly renewals fan-out only. ⚠️ This binding is the thing that does NOT scale: a 50-app portfolio cannot carry 50 hand-added D1 bindings on one Worker. Recorded here so the next app's stamp meets the ceiling as a known cost rather than as a surprise ([4]B-11 derives the job set; the fan-out target list is still `appTargets()`'s hardcoded array).

A stamped app's own private database — the only datastore an opt-in backend owns outright. D1 Free is 10 databases per account and platform_db is one of them, which is why a backend is opt-in rather than default ([ADR 020]).
Per-app CFG-1 config overrides, keyed `config:<app>`, read on the launch path of every app and edge-cached for 300s.
Caches the Supabase JWKS document so an ES256 verify does not fetch it per request. One identity project portfolio-wide, so one cache.

The `nikatru-signups` namespace, bound READ-ONLY into `platform` for the nightly off-vendor export and NOTHING else. 🔴 `research/revamp-2026-09-05/06 §3.4` measured it bound to no Worker at all — 2 list operations, 0 reads, 0 writes in seven days — which is the exact shape of a store that gets lost with nobody noticing, and it holds contactable email addresses. The writer is still sites/nikatru/functions/api/subscribe.js (a Pages Function), which is also where its expirationTtl is set; this Worker never writes it. A binding is the only way a Worker can back up a namespace.

The ONE portfolio backup bucket, `nikatru-backups`, written by the 02:30 cron only and addressed by key prefix (`d1/`, `kv/`, `manifests/`). 🔴 It closes `06 §4.2` — D1, KV and R2 in NO backup, `recovery.worker-d1-export` NEVER drilled — for the entitlements database that serves the whole portfolio. ⚠️ It is deliberately ONE bucket: the per-app `<app>-exports` buckets removed from the brick on 2026-07-25 are the precedent, and the live app's own per-app binding was removed on 2026-08-01 (the NO r2_buckets comment in services/subscriptiontracker-api/wrangler.jsonc).

FAIRNESS bucket for /v1/events + /v1/consent, keyed `(app_id, anon_id)`. ⚠️ That key is ENTIRELY client-chosen on a route that is unauthenticated by design, so it bounds one honest install and nothing more — EVENTS_CEILING_LIMITER is the half a caller cannot rotate out of.
SERVER-DERIVED ceiling for /v1/events + /v1/consent, keyed `edge:<colo>:<asn>` from `request.cf` — no request-body value is in the key. Its own namespace so it cannot spend the fairness budget.

The same server-derived ceiling for GET /config/:app — the other unauthenticated route on this Worker that does I/O. Its own namespace so config traffic and analytics traffic cannot exhaust each other.

The server-derived ceiling for POST /v1/money/:provider, keyed `edge:<colo>:<asn>`. Its OWN namespace so a flood of forged notifications cannot exhaust the budget analytics ingest and config resolution depend on — both of those are on every app's LAUNCH path, so borrowing from them would let anyone who finds this URL degrade the whole portfolio.

⏱ 2026-09-24 · O-EXTENSION-ACCOUNT-CHECK-UNBUILT. The server-derived ceiling for POST /v1/ext/token, keyed `edge:<colo>:<asn>` — never an IP. `simple: { limit: 60, period: 60 }`: one exchange per sign-in, room for a shared NAT, and the end of a flood against a 128-bit code. Its OWN namespace (1005) so a code-guessing flood cannot spend the budget analytics ingest, config resolution or the money rail depend on.
